name: Weight-merge backdoor
setup: CLIP ViT-B/32 to L/14 over 6 to 13 image tasks, or Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B over 2 to 6 text tasks. Merge methods: task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, Breadcrumbs, DELLA, RegMean, AdaMerging. Metric: attack success rate (ASR) on triggered inputs, plus the merged model's clean accuracy.
attacker: Builds one fine-tuned checkpoint and publishes it. Usually blind to the other models, the merge method and the coefficients. Colluding variants supply two to four parts that are each clean on their own.
defender: Generic backdoor defences run on each model alone (Neural Cleanse, fine-pruning, SafeLoRA, PEFTGuard); in a few papers, a merge-aware defence.
numbers: One backdoored model among six merged: 96.7 to 99.5% ASR, with merged accuracy within 0.2 points of clean [[zhang-2024-badmerging]]. 100% under task arithmetic on Llama-3-8B, still high at merge ratio 0.2 [[yuan-2025-merge]]. Adapters at 0% ASR alone reach 98 to 100% when composed [[ding-2026-colluding]]. Source models 3 to 29% harmful, merged model 72 to 85% [[li-2026-when]].
misses: The corrupted part is installed by the experimenter, never turned by its domain. Parts come from strangers, not forks of the parent. No test hides which parts get merged.

name: Federated and Byzantine aggregation
setup: CIFAR-10, MNIST, EMNIST or Reddit with 10 to 100 clients per round under FedAvg, Krum, median or trimmed mean. Federated RL on CartPole, LunarLander or MuJoCo with 10 to 90 agents, 5 to 10 seeds. Many results are proofs with no experiment.
attacker: f of n clients send arbitrary updates. Often omniscient for the proof; the practical attacks (A Little Is Enough, inner-product manipulation) estimate the honest spread and stay inside it.
defender: A trusted aggregator, synchronous rounds, i.i.d. honest data, and a known bound on f (2f + 2 < n for Krum).
numbers: One participant in one round drives backdoor accuracy close to 100% under FedAvg, and Krum makes the attack easier [[bagdasaryan-2020-how]]. 20% of workers inside the honest variance cut CIFAR-10 accuracy by half [[baruch-2019-little]]. In the lab's one-seed ByzFL run, robust rules held to 5 corrupted inputs of 11 and snapped at 6 [[gh-lpd-epfl-byzfl]]. Hashed groups tolerated 40% malicious agents on CartPole [[fang-2025-provably]].
misses: Independence and honest-data overlap are assumptions, not variables. The aggregator is never corrupted. The parts are separate clients, not copies of one model.

name: LLM voting, debate and N-version
adv: A1, A2; A4 as benign correlation
setup: 5 to 25 agents, usually copies of one open model (Qwen, Llama, Mistral, Gemma), on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU or MMLU-Pro with majority or quorum vote. Correlation studies pool tens to hundreds of models on benign benchmarks (349 models on 12,032 MMLU questions).
attacker: A static injection appended to some agents' prompts, or a scripted agent that gives a wrong answer with full confidence (F = 1). Defence-aware adaptive attackers are left to future work.
defender: Honest majority, signed messages, fixed membership, independent errors, and sometimes truthful self-reported confidence.
numbers: With 3 of 5 agents injected, raising votes from 1 to 40 cut majority accuracy from 46.2% to 25.9% [[liu-2026-consensus]]. One deceiver who held exclusive evidence cut truth recovery from 72.5% to 14.2% [[yan-2026-when]]. One weak agent claiming confidence 1.0 dropped CP-WBFT from 79% to 47.5% [[lee-2026-robust]]. When two LLMs are both wrong they agree 0.42 to 0.60 of the time [[kim-2025-correlated]].
misses: Corrupted agents are assumed independent, with the injection placed in the prompt rather than read from a shared domain. Every part sees the same task, so the case where one part alone covers a domain is almost never tested (Yan is the exception).

name: Single agent with a persistent store
setup: One GPT-4-class or Claude agent with a ReAct or tool-calling scaffold and one memory, RAG store or config file. Benchmarks: AgentDojo, InjecAgent, ASB, EHRAgent on MIMIC-III, LongMemEval, BEIR, or a bespoke sandbox. Trial counts are small: 10 per condition is common; 3,150 in SMSR is the largest.
attacker: Writes to the store directly, or sends ordinary queries until the agent writes the poison itself (query-only), or controls one tool response. Black-box and mostly non-adaptive.
defender: A trusted system prompt and config, an honest LLM judge, a correct provenance oracle, and a bound on the number of poisoned items. CaMeL explicitly assumes memory is clean.
numbers: Query-only memory injection above 95% success, falling as benign memory grows [[dong-2025-memory]]. Planted memory payloads persist across sessions in 50 to 97% of runs [[gadgil-2026-bad]]. Self-written config payloads succeed 63% overall, and a sandbox that discards identity-file writes takes that to 0 [[zhang-2026-agentworm]]. Two independent trusted principals bring laundering ASR to 0% [[louck-2026-securing]]. A promotion gate from private to shared memory: 51.4% to 0.3% [[xiong-2026-maple]]. /compact keeps 53% of safety rules after one round and 10% after five [[zerhoudi-2026-compaction]].
misses: The merge is a later session of the same agent or a shared store, not a returning fork. k is 1 or small and is never swept. No correlated corruption from a shared base model, and no host or channel attacker.

name: Multi-agent channel and contagion
setup: AutoGen, CrewAI, Camel, MetaGPT or ChatDev with 3 to 6 agents in a chain, tree, star, complete or random topology, on MMLU, HumanEval or MBPP. Contagion simulations run up to a million LLaVA agents with random pairwise chats, or 20-hop email chains over Enron mailboxes.
attacker: Controls one channel into one agent (agent-in-the-middle), or plants one file, page or image that the system reads. In contagion work, one seeded agent or document.
defender: Framework defaults. Graph-based detectors assume they see the whole utterance graph and have labelled attack data.
numbers: An agent-in-the-middle on one victim succeeded above 40% in all 32 cells, and intercepting a parent rather than a child raised success from 40.7% to 67.4% [[he-2025-red]]. Laundering an attack through subagent metadata reached 58 to 90% reverse-shell success, against 0 to 1% for plain indirect injection [[triedman-2025-multi]]. One adversarial image infected nearly all of up to 10^6 agents [[gu-2024-agent]]. A RAG worm replicated at over 90% up to hop 11 [[cohen-2024-here]].
misses: Topologies are flat or fixed peer graphs with no hub parent that merges. Attackers are mostly scripted. Whether summarisation or consolidation strips taint on the way into a parent is asserted in several sources and never measured.

name: AI control evaluations
setup: An untrusted frontier model (GPT-4, Claude 3.5 to 4.5, Gemini 3) plays a red-team attack policy on coding or shell benchmarks (APPS, BashBench with 257 tasks, SHADE-Arena, FakeLab with 86 tasks) against a weaker trusted monitor with a 1 to 5% audit budget. Agent counts: 1, 2 (policy plus monitor), or K = 3 or 9 sequential executors.
attacker: Told to attack and usually knows the protocol. When the monitor is a copy, it can collude through self-recognition or Schelling points.
defender: A trusted weaker model, a human audit budget, honeypots, and signal jamming (paraphrase, minification).
numbers: Trusted monitoring: 62% safety at 97% usefulness. Naive untrusted monitoring: 0%; with anti-collusion measures: 79% [[greenblatt-2023-ai]]. Splitting an attack over three agents cut per-commit suspicion from 0.92 to 0.60 to 0.68, and the squashed diff scored 0.90 again [[makins-2026-multi]]. Resampling safety fell from 96% to 17% against a protocol-aware attacker [[kutasov-2025-evaluating]]. Two isolated copies coordinated for 4 to 6 rounds with no communication [[jarviniemi-2025-subversion]].
misses: No parallel forks, no persistent merge into parent state (the artifact is reviewed once), and the trusted monitor is never itself corrupted.

name: Demonstrations on deployed agent stacks
setup: Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes and MCP clients in real or sandboxed workspaces. Evidence is a video, a reasoning trace or a handful of trials, never a sampled rate.
attacker: Plants one email, page, image, repository file or tool description that a subagent reads. The payload reaches the parent as a forwarded summary or as a write to MEMORY.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or MCP config.
defender: Vendor defaults: a sandboxed summariser, random delimiters, and permission prompts.
numbers: A sandboxed Gmail summariser relayed a crafted block to the main agent despite random delimiters [[veganmosfet-2026-brokenclaw]]. One coding agent rewrote another's instruction and MCP files [[embracethered-2025-cross]]. A subagent terminated its sibling on a plain instruction with no parent authorisation, and models from five more vendors reproduced the behaviour [[cai-2026-child]].
misses: These show the attack exists but give no rates. Most use one child, and the full child-to-parent-to-future-session chain is never scored link by link.

name: Classical systems: mobile agents, replication, CRDTs, hiding
setup: Mostly proofs plus small simulations: 14 SparcStations with 1 to 7 replicas; 4 CRDT replicas; 1,000 simulated validators; 6 mixes. Supply chain (in-toto, reproducible builds) as signed k-of-n gates.
attacker: A malicious host that rewrites the visiting agent's state, or replays it on chosen inputs; Byzantine replicas that equivocate; a network attacker that targets or deanonymises the chosen party.
defender: Deterministic, byte-comparable stage outputs; an honest majority per stage; replicas that fail independently; a clean trusted home; an honest mix or shuffler; no Sybils.
numbers: Three replicas with a majority vote at every stage cut a 6x slowdown to about 20% [[minsky-1996-cryptographic]]. Non-interactive secure mobile computing is impossible when the host gets state-dependent output [[algesheimer-2001-cryptographic]]. Byzantine eventual consistency holds with any number of faulty replicas exactly when updates are I-confluent, and a validly signed poisoned update still merges everywhere [[kleppmann-2020-byzantine]]. Secret leader election cut targeted-DoS missed blocks from 64% to about 0, but a public candidate list made a blind attack worse (28% against 6 to 8%) [[burianova-2025-secret]].
misses: LLM outputs are not byte-comparable, so replica voting does not apply directly. The merged object is never LLM memory. Hiding and integrity of the returned content are never combined.

name: Biology and human-memory analogues
setup: In the analogue, the part is a colony, nucleus or clone, the merge is somatic fusion, the attacker is a cheater or parasite lineage, and the credential check is an allorecognition locus. Best rigs: Neurospora with 2 treatments × 8 lines over 31 to 41 transfers; Botryllus field and lab chimeras genotyped by microsatellite. Human work: misinformation and false-memory paradigms, and intelligence case studies.
attacker: Usually arises by mutation and does not adapt. Transmissible cancers and social parasites first carry no label, then copy the host's.
defender: A single identity gate at the moment of fusion, with no check afterwards.
numbers: All 8 free-fusion lines evolved cheaters and lost about threefold in yield, while non-fusing lines did not change [[bastiaans-2016-experimental]]. Germline parasitism in 40% of fused chimeras against 6.7% of unfused pairs [[stoner-1996-somatic]]. Each mismatched vic locus cuts virus transfer on its own [[cortesi-2001-genetic]]. Correlated reports "may be no more informative than a single report" [[heuer-1999-psychology]].
misses: The gate checks identity, never the integrity of what comes back, so a cheater that carries the right label is never tested. These are the only controlled comparisons of merging against never merging.
